title: Decoder loop preserves free variables
statement: Fix a number of variables $n$, and let $D$ denote the recursive loop underlying Razborov's decoder, which takes as input a DNF formula $f$ on $n$ variables, a width parameter $w \in \bbn$, a fuel bound $\mathrm{fuel} \in \bbn$, two restrictions $\sigma$ and $\rho_0$ on the $n$ variables, and an auxiliary list of index–value pairs drawn from $\bbn \times \mathrm{Bool}$, and returns a pair whose first component is again a restriction on the $n$ variables. Then for every variable $v$ with $\sigma(v) = \mathrm{none}$, the first component of $D(f, w, \mathrm{fuel}, \sigma, \rho_0, \mathrm{aux})$ also assigns $\mathrm{none}$ to $v$.
hypotheses_covered: f is a DNF formula on n variables
w is a natural-number width parameter
σ and ρ₀ are restrictions on the n variables
aux is a list of index–value (ℕ × Bool) pairs
v is a variable with σ(v) = none
caveat: The declaration concerns an internal auxiliary recursion (razborovDecode.go) whose actual computation is not part of the supplied material, so the prose faithfully states the invariant (variables left free by σ remain free in the output restriction) but cannot make the loop's internal behaviour self-contained; the roles of w, fuel, ρ₀, and aux are named but not otherwise specified.
replaced:
If $\sigma\,v = \mathrm{none}$, then the decoder loop
\texttt{SwitchingLemma2.razborovDecode}'s \texttt{go} leaves $v$ unset; its resulting
$\sigma$ is still $\mathrm{none}$ at $v$.
